definitions.explanation: Describes something or someone that is fresh, new, or full of youthful energy. From English 'fresh.' Often used for new employees, fresh produce, or a refreshing impression.

examples.japanese: フレッシュな{気持|きも}ち⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{始|はじ}めよう→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
examples.english: Let's start with a fresh mindset.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧フレッシュマン⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: This year's new recruits are full of energy.

examples.japanese: フレッシュな⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}った→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦サラダ→サラダ：01364_sarada⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦やっぱり→やっぱり：03005_yappari⟧⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧。
examples.english: A salad made with fresh vegetables really does taste good.

notes:
A loanword from English used as a na-adjective (フレッシュな). In Japanese, this word emphasizes newness and youthful vitality more than freshness of food — though it can be used for food as well.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- フレッシュな⟦{人材|じんざい}→人材：11426_jinzai⟧: fresh talent
- フレッシュマン: new employee; freshman (wasei-eigo)
- フレッシュな⟦{印象|いんしょう}→印象：01846_inshou⟧: fresh impression
- フレッシュな{気持|きも}ち: fresh feeling; renewed spirit
- フレッシュ⟦ジュース→ジュース：01033_juusu⟧: freshly squeezed juice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{新鮮|しんせん}→新鮮：03261_shinsen⟧: fresh — the native Japanese equivalent, used more broadly for food freshness and novel experiences
- ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧: new — general word for newness without the youthful energy nuance
- ⟦{若々|わかわか}しい→若々しい：18038_wakawakashii⟧: youthful — focuses specifically on youthful appearance or energy
